facts.claim: First satellite detection of a milky sea was reported in 2005
12 milky-sea events found 2012-2021 over the Indian Ocean and far western Pacific
Leading idea: luminous bacteria on algae; still a hypothesis

lines.text: Sailors have told of nights when the sea turned white.
Not waves. Not moonlight. A silent glow, from the ship to the horizon.
It sounds like a sailor's ghost story.
Satellites have photographed it from space: about a dozen glowing seas in nine years, over the Indian Ocean and the western Pacific.
The leading idea: billions of glowing bacteria living on algae, all shining at once.
But it's still an idea. No one knows for sure what switches it on.
So if you ever wake to a white, silent sea, you might be floating on one of the biggest light shows on Earth.
